key_insight: VIME uses classical imaginary-time pre-training plus a compressed ansatz to prepare molecular ground states with much lower quantum resource cost than prior variational Majorana methods.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets near-term fault-tolerant quantum chemistry by cutting CNOT count and two-qubit depth while preserving chemically accurate energies on challenging correlated molecules.
method: Extends OVQITE to molecular electronic structure via a single compiled Majorana-propagation surrogate graph
Pairs the algorithm with a compressed tiled Unitary Product State (c-tUPS) ansatz to reduce simulation and state-preparation cost
Uses classical pre-training before quantum execution to improve hardware efficiency
evidence_signal: On TLD-1411 and acene benchmarks up to 60 qubits, VIME reaches chemical precision and matches or improves ADAPT-VMPE accuracy with up to 26× fewer CNOTs and 167× lower two-qubit depth.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the surrogate graph, ansatz compression, and active-space setup, so benefits may vary across molecules and hardware constraints.
paper_title: Hardware-Efficient Ground-State Preparation using Variational Imaginary-Time Majorana Evolution
